name: Memento-Skills: Let Agents Design Agents
authors: Huichi Zhou et al. (Memento-Team), lead affiliation University College London (UCL); 17 authors including Jun Wang (UCL); other contributors from Jilin University, HKUST(GZ), and the AI Lab of the Yangtze River Delta.
feedback_source: self-generated (LLM-as-judge verdict + diagnostic execution traces); a synthetic unit-test gate verifies rewritten skills; in benchmark training the judge is scored against ground-truth answers (GAIA/HLE have verifiable answers)
iteration_structure: iterative-refine (closed-loop Read-Write loop: Observe -> Read -> Act -> Feedback -> Write, with up to K=3 reflective retries per task and multiple training rounds R0-R3); population-like skill-library growth across episodes
reflection_object: Primarily reusable skill/workflow artefacts ('skill folders' = SKILL.md declarative spec + helper scripts + prompts), plus the prompt/context (stateful prompt and a 'tip memory'). Adaptation also targets the agent's own code (executable skill code) and the routing policy, but never the LLM weights.
learning_locus: in_context_verbal (no weight update) — described by the authors as 'continual learning without updating LLM parameters'; the only gradient training is on the small external skill-router embedding model, not the policy LLM, so it is effectively non-parametric for the agent policy
requires_training: none for the policy LLM (frozen). The skill router is trained with single-step offline RL (multi-positive InfoNCE contrastive fine-tuning) on top of a Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B model; no RL/SFT on the generative LLM.
reward_or_critic_model: self-as-judge (LLM-as-a-judge, MT-bench style) provides the CORRECT/INCORRECT signal driving reflection; for the router, a verifiable reward r(q,d) (whether retrieved skill is the right tool) defines a one-step soft Q-function
distillation_target: reusable-skill/workflow — reflection is consolidated into executable, multi-artefact skills (markdown spec + code + prompts) stored as persistent external memory; also accumulates a prompt-level 'tip memory'
emergent_vs_engineered: prompt/scaffold-engineered — the reflective behaviour is an explicitly designed Read-Write loop (failure-attribution selector, skill rewriter, skill-discovery escalation, unit-test gate). It is not RL-emergent 'aha' reasoning; the only learned-by-gradient component is the external router embedding.
memory_type: skill-library (external, writable; SKILL.md + helper scripts + prompts), augmented by a short prompt-level tip memory
memory_persistence: cross-task and cross-session (production) — skills persist in an external library that grows over time and is reused across tasks and deployments without retraining
memory_curation_mechanism: overwrite/evolution (self-relinking) — Write actively mutates skills: failure attribution selects the responsible skill, skill rewriter applies targeted in-place edits, and when a skill's running utility drops below threshold delta the system escalates to skill discovery (restructure or synthesize new skill); a utility table tracks empirical success rate, and an automatic unit-test gate validates and rolls back regressive mutations (retrieval-gated read via behaviour-aligned router)
error_localization_granularity: agent-level / skill-level — an LLM-based failure attribution selector inspects the full execution trace and judge rationale to identify the single skill most responsible for the error (skill-level credit assignment), then patches that skill
intra_task_vs_inter_task: inter-task — refined skills transfer across tasks; the paper shows cross-task transfer is strongest when the skill library aligns with the benchmark's domain structure (e.g., a skill refined on one Biology question is reused for unseen Biology questions on HLE; weaker on diverse GAIA)
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: mixed: post-hoc-revision plus within-task mid-trajectory recovery — after a failed attempt the agent rewrites the skill and retries (up to K reflective rounds 5b-5d) on the same task, and the revised skills also avoid the failure mode on future tasks
task_domains: general (general AI assistant tasks), QA/reasoning across academic subjects, tool-use, web-navigation/search, multi-modality, terminal/code operations; agent-designing (meta-agent that builds task-specific agents)
benchmarks: GAIA (General AI Assistants; 165 validation questions split 100 train / 65 test) and HLE (Humanity's Last Exam; subset of 788 train / 342 test from 2,500 questions across 8 subjects); router evaluated on 140 synthetic routing queries
headline_result: On GAIA test set, full Memento-Skills reaches 66.0% accuracy vs 52.3% for the static Read-Write baseline (+13.7 pp, 26.2% relative); on HLE test set, 38.7% vs 17.9% (+20.8 pp, 116.2% relative, more than doubling the baseline). Base LLM: Gemini-3.1-Flash.
baselines: A 'Read-Write' ablation that keeps the same read-write loop (skill retrieval + LLM execution + feedback) but disables all skill-level optimisation (no failure attribution, no skill rewriting, no skill discovery). Router baselines: BM25 (sparse) and Qwen3-Embedding (dense semantic).
gains_vs_baseline: GAIA test +13.7 pp (66.0% vs 52.3%, 26.2% relative); HLE test +20.8 pp (38.7% vs 17.9%, 116.2% relative). Training-time gains: GAIA 65.1% -> 91.6% over 3 retry rounds; HLE 30.8% (R0) -> 54.5% (R3). Router: Recall@1 0.60 vs 0.54 (Qwen3) and 0.32 (BM25); route hit rate 0.58 vs 0.53/0.29; judge success rate 0.80 vs 0.79 (Qwen3) and 0.50 (BM25).
compute_cost_profile: Zero retraining / zero gradient updates to the policy LLM; adaptation cost is the external skill memory plus router fine-tuning. Inference cost includes up to K=3 reflective retries per training question (extra LLM calls + judge + unit-test execution) plus retrieval over a growing skill library; router training uses ~5k crawled skills with ~3k sampled as seed for synthetic query generation. Authors emphasise '$400 in compute to learn nothing' from fine-tuning vs near-zero retraining cost; reported production figures (illustrative dialogue) ~195ms p99 latency, 93.5% accuracy.
known_limitations: Limited cross-task transfer when tasks are highly diverse (on GAIA most training-optimised skills were never triggered at test time because no similar test question existed); transfer depends on domain alignment. Diminishing returns as the skill library saturates (memory coverage radius shrinks). Some domains saturate early/low (HLE Engineering plateaus at ~42.1%) suggesting skill-level abstraction is insufficient for certain domains. Sandbox safety / isolation (whether skills run without breaking the environment) is explicitly left to future work. Embedding similarity is a poor proxy for behavioural utility (motivating the trained router).
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: external-tool/verifier plus oracle-label on benchmarks: improvement relies on an LLM-as-judge verdict and a synthetic unit-test gate; on GAIA/HLE the judge effectively uses the benchmark's unambiguous ground-truth answers during training rounds, so reported training gains depend on verifiable-answer feedback. The router uses a verifiable reward (correct-skill label).
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive (task-dependent) — skill optimisation adds +13.7 pp (GAIA) and +20.8 pp (HLE) over the no-optimisation baseline; ablation removing skill optimisation drops accuracy (~8% in the reported case) and removing the trained router causes retrieval collapse. Gains are largest where domain-aligned skill reuse is possible.
failure_attribution_capability: attributes-responsible-agent / attributes-failing-step — an LLM-based failure attribution selector examines the full execution trace and judge rationale to identify the single skill most responsible for the error and performs skill-level credit assignment before targeted rewriting
failure_mode_addressed: Targets task-execution failures via skill-level credit assignment and patching: superficial/insufficient skill specifications, brittle narrowly-scoped skills, and routing errors where semantically-similar-but-behaviourally-wrong skills are retrieved (curse of embedding similarity). Adds guardrails / alternative strategies for observed failure modes while preserving generality; escalates to new-skill discovery when in-place patching is insufficient.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: Yes — an open-sourced curated skill dataset/marketplace (https://skills.memento.run/market/) built from public GitHub skills (filtered to >500 stars, SHA-256 dedup), plus code at https://github.com/Memento-Teams/Memento-Skills. No new evaluation benchmark released (uses existing GAIA and HLE).
builds_on: Memento 2 (Stateful Reflective Decision Process / Read-Write Reflective Learning, Reflected MDP and KL-regularised soft policy iteration convergence theorem) [wang2025memento2]; Memento: Fine-tuning LLM agents without fine-tuning LLMs (Zhou et al. 2025); case-based-reasoning LLM agents DS-Agent and functional test-script generation (Guo et al.); LLM-as-a-judge (MT-Bench, Zheng et al.); Qwen3-Embedding; BM25. Conceptually related to GEPA (reflective prompt evolution) and Letta skill learning, which it contrasts itself against.
reasoning_model_native: no — the method is model-agnostic and applied to a frozen general LLM (Gemini-3.1-Flash); reflection is externalised in skills/prompts rather than relying on a built-in reasoning/'aha' mechanism of an o1/R1-style model
on_policy_distillation_link: Strong conceptual link: routing is cast as single-step OFFLINE RL (one-step soft Q-learning / KL-regularised Boltzmann policy) deliberately because the on-policy exploration space is too sparse (~8k skills, few hundred tasks). Reflection distills experience into reusable executable skills (skill optimisation) rather than into model weights, an alternative to on-policy distillation that updates externalised behaviour instead of parameters.
sample_efficiency: High in episode terms: substantial gains within 3-4 training rounds (GAIA 65.1%->91.6% over 3 retries; HLE 30.8%->54.5% over R0-R3) using only 100 (GAIA) / 788 (HLE) training questions and 5 atomic seed skills, with zero policy-LLM gradient steps. Library grows from 5 seed skills to 41 (GAIA) / 235 (HLE). Authors note diminishing returns ~O(n^{-1/d}) as coverage saturates.
